### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in handleInstall; a string literal in unmanagedInstallRenameRefusal))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in handleInstall; a string literal in unmanagedInstallRenameRefusal))_

- `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx`  _(via targetNamespace (symbol, a field of interface NamespaceRename; a field of interface NamespaceRenameInput), INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in handleInstall; a string literal in unmanagedInstallRenameRefusal))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1fb8b9b7a262ab8aa2595032495546e16a165a68` — the merge of head `cacc28d42ca4d7a23c170f9877869be5a0d40761` into base `7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1fb8b9b7a262ab8aa2595032495546e16a165a68 && git checkout 1fb8b9b7a262ab8aa2595032495546e16a165a68
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544 cacc28d42ca4d7a23c170f9877869be5a0d40761 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544 && git merge --no-ff cacc28d42ca4d7a23c170f9877869be5a0d40761

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7d9f1e973ecc418c21736a58da2eb211f08a3544` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b377514f88d5e040ca98878bcde829b0fb834a4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts + packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-namespace-rename.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-namespace-rename.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-install-modes.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-unmanaged-import-rename-battery.test.ts, .changeset/30794-unmanaged-install-target-namespace.md, packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (cited: the namespace rule), scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs (cited: the red gate)

Diff read against merge-base `1aeeafd9` (origin/main at the head's plain merge): 14 files, +1966/−361. Card #30794 body and all 7 comments read (claim 6676579365 amended 6676622319, spec consent 6688079820, os-dev-report 6689472616). PR body read. Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accepted set and public surface, one line each. "Confirmed" means read in the cited code at the head.

**Spec hunk (the consented face)**
- `ImportUnmanagedPackageRequestSchema` gains `targetNamespace?: string` (package-lifecycle.zod.ts:408). The schema is `.strict()`, so a body carrying the key was refused before and is accepted now. Widening. Exactly the key consent 6688079820 names. **Correct.**
- `ImportUnmanagedPackageResponseSchema` gains `sourceNamespace?: string` (:445) and `namespace`'s describe now covers the renamed case (:441). Exactly the second consented key. The code emits `sourceNamespace` only when a rename happened (protocol-package-commits.ts:721), so the old answer's key set is unchanged; pinned by "answers no `sourceNamespace`" in package-unmanaged-install.test.ts. **Correct.**
- `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`: exactly two added rows, `api/ImportUnmanagedPackageRequest:targetNamespace` and `api/ImportUnmanagedPackageResponse:sourceNamespace`, nothing else. That is precisely what two optional keys imply. The reference page `content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx` gains the two rows and the re-described `namespace` row. "Spec property liveness" and `Check Changeset` are green on the head. **Consistent.**
- No other published surface owed a change: the install-local door's body is not a strict spec schema (only `installMode` is parsed through `InstallModeSchema`, marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1798); `installedFrom` appears in no `packages/spec/src` schema. **Confirmed.**

**Scope against the claim (6676622319)**
- Files touched: `packages/metadata-protocol/**`, `packages/cloud-connection/**`, `packages/objectql/**` (the replay of the duplicate battery, named in the claim's surface), `content/docs/**`, one root `.changeset/`, and `packages/spec/**` under the consent. No `ui/**`, `skills/**`, `.claude/**`, no CLI file. **Inside the claim.**

**Correctness**
- One engine, not a fork: `planNamespaceRename` (package-namespace-rename.ts:142) is the duplicate's inline body moved whole; the diff of protocol-package-commits.ts removes the inline rename (−290 lines) and calls the engine (:288–302, `retryVerb: 'duplicate'`), reading `copyName` (:325, :400), `objectRefusal` (:395) and `rewrite` (:467). The import calls the same function (package-unmanaged-install.ts:541–547, `retryVerb: 'install'`; protocol-package-commits.ts:655). `REFERENCE_SITES` import moved with it. **Confirmed; no second copy.**
- duplicatePackage's behaviour is unchanged except one case: `copyName` (:450–457) now maps a `view` row whose bare name IS a renamed object's name to that object's copy name (`ticket` → `dupdst_ticket`). Before, `renameName` kept `ticket`. This is a widening fix someone could meet: a duplicate of a base holding a bare object and its container. The old result stored the copy's container under the source's name (shadowed by name), the new result stores it beside the copied object. No refusal is added to the duplicate: `copyNameRefusal` is import-only (:472, docblock :82–84), and the ADR-0086 D3 `packageId` rebind stays in the duplicate (:483). The four `protocol-duplicate-package-*` files are untouched. **Confirmed; a fix, not a narrowing.** The changeset names it ("A bare object's view container follows it on a duplicate too").
- Order and no write before refusal (import): request parse (400) → walled posture (409, :574) → plan: namespace rule (`ManifestSchema.shape.namespace.safeParse`, package-unmanaged-install.ts:480, regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$`), reserved `base`/`system`/`sys` (:488, `PLATFORM_RESERVED_NAMESPACES` :103) → targetPackageId → item enumeration with containers expanded → rename refusals on names (claimed object, grammar `METADATA_ITEM_NAME_PATTERN`, 63 for objects, 255 for any item; :540–558, engine :472–493) → owned-namespace 409 on the TARGET namespace (:607) → convert then `rewrite`; a reference/key collision throws `INVALID_REQUEST` 400 (:655–670) → same-name 409 over the RENAMED names and expansions (:673). The base is installed after all of that. **Confirmed.**
- Codes: rename refusals `INVALID_REQUEST` 400 with `details.refused[]` (:602–620); collisions and owned namespace `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` 409; the door's managed+`targetNamespace` refusal `INVALID_REQUEST` 400 before any fetch (door :1817–1827). The namespace-rule and reserved refusals use `invalidRequest` (:285): `statusCode: 400` and NO `code`, which the boundary answers as `VALIDATION_ERROR` — the dev's own test pins `[400, 'VALIDATION_ERROR']`. See ③ (should-fix: the prose says `INVALID_REQUEST`).
- Idempotency: a second import with the same `targetNamespace` meets the first copy's base as the namespace owner (409 at :607) and, by default, the same `targetPackageId` (existing 409). Nothing is merged or renamed a second time. **Confirmed.**
- Translations are `<targetNamespace>_<locale>` with object keys inside renamed (planner test pins `unmanagedTranslationItemName('acme','zh-CN')`; engine renames record keys at reference sites :347). **Confirmed.**

**Security / tenancy**
- A chosen `targetNamespace` cannot take another package's names: the registry's `getNamespaceOwners` refusal (code packages and writable bases alike, :607) plus the per-name `unmanagedImportCollisions` over every renamed name and expansion against environment rows of any package and managed artifacts (protocol.ts:11990). Both run before the base exists. Pinned by "refuses a target namespace another package owns" and "judges collisions on the RENAMED names". **Confirmed.**
- Cross-org: the import is refused on a walled posture (:574, unchanged) and writes environment rows with no organization. `targetNamespace` adds no org-crossing path. **Confirmed.**
- The value is judged by the manifest's own regex before it reaches any identifier, so no table name can carry an unexpected character. Reserved namespaces refused. **Confirmed.**

**Tests and ablations**
- Parity (package-unmanaged-install.test.ts, "the rename parity") stores identical active rows through duplicate and import. The 8 planner + 8 import cases pin each refusal's status and code. The engine file has 6 cases including the container rule (package-namespace-rename.test.ts:67–81). The door has 3 cases (forwarded, unchanged without, refused beside managed/default with no fetch/import/register/ledger). The objectql replay (9 cases) runs both doors on a real kernel and asserts equality of stored items and each refusal. Removing the engine call, the planner branch, either limit, the reserved check, the collision judgement on renamed names, or the door's forward would make named assertions fail; the 17 ablation rows are consistent with what the tests assert. **Read as red-on-removal.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec`: `minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `patch`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`: `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` in the PR body and the changeset, both at line start. **Right.** `added` is required here: the authorable-surface baseline moved (api.json), which `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` forbids beside `none`; the kind must grade at least ONE moved package `minor`, and spec is. Precedent: `GetMetaItemLayeredRequest.member` shipped `Metadata-protocol: added` for an API request key. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is present in the PR body as SKILL.md:313 requires for a kind other than `none`; the reason holds (the only `skills/**` hit is a plugin-name listing in operations.md:110; no skill teaches `installMode` or an unmanaged copy). `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q6 (not ruled here, assessed for landing safety).** Step 1f (door :2286, `findEnvironmentBaseHoldingNamespace` :3910) is untouched: it refuses a managed install when a WRITABLE base holds the package's declared namespace. Before this PR every unmanaged copy held the source namespace, so "same source package" and "same namespace" were the same test. After it, a RENAMED copy holds `targetNamespace`, so a later managed install of the source package is not refused by 1f. Assessment: this is not a regression and not a narrowing of an existing guarantee. Every pre-existing state (an unrenamed copy) is refused exactly as before, and the harm 1f guards against — the package's definitions taking over the copy's names at the next boot — cannot happen to a renamed copy, whose items carry different names. What is left unguarded is only the new capability's own edge (a policy question: should "same source package" be refused regardless of names). Landing PR A without the ruling is safe; the maintainer's answer (B, A or C) changes nothing already shipped. No test pins either outcome, as the PR says.
- **Should-fix (prose faces, for the lane seat's ACCEPT): the error code named for a refused or reserved `targetNamespace`.** The changeset ("answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST`") and `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx` (new refusal row "`400 INVALID_REQUEST`, naming `targetNamespace`") name `INVALID_REQUEST`, but package-unmanaged-install.ts:480–495 throws through `invalidRequest` (:285), which carries `statusCode: 400` and no `code`; the boundary answers `VALIDATION_ERROR`, and the PR's own planner test asserts exactly that. The same shape the existing `targetPackageId` refusal has. Either give those two throws `code: 'INVALID_REQUEST'` (then the sibling rename refusal at :610 and the door at :1818 agree) or correct the two prose claims. Not in the spec hunk (the describe names no code), so not a contract must-fix.
- **Landing condition ② is not met on this head: two red check-runs.** `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` fails at the `Test-source alias gate` step (its "source reach" half), and `Lint & Repo Gates` is the lane aggregator of the same failure. Finding, verbatim from the job log: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts:45: reaches import('@objectstack/lint') in the source under test, at packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts:494`, reached during collection through `package-unmanaged-install.test.ts → protocol.ts → metadata-diagnostics.ts`, with no module-top load of `@objectstack/lint` in the test and the package resolving it through `dist/`. The half judges only test files a change adds or edits; this file is edited by the PR (its line-45 import of `./protocol.js` is old, but the file is now in the judged set). The merge-base's lint lane is green, so this is not a same-signature red. Remedy, as the gate prints it: add `import '@objectstack/lint';` at module top of `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`. Test-only, one line; the new head then takes a delta review by this reviewer (the change is neither regen nor prose). The other three test files carry no dynamic `import()`/`require()` and import only what sibling tests already import, so they trip neither half.
- **The door refuses `targetNamespace` beside a managed install (400).** The door's body is not a strict published schema, so a managed body carrying that key was silently ignored before and is refused now. It is a refusal on a key no published contract declared, not a narrowing of a declared surface; recorded so nobody rediscovers it.
- **Three spellings of the reserved namespaces** (`PLATFORM_RESERVED_NAMESPACES`, objectql's `RESERVED_NAMESPACES`, the door's inline check in `findEnvironmentBaseHoldingNamespace`). All read `base`/`system`/`sys` today. Drift risk only; the dev noted it, outside the card.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login to name.
- `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 30997`: 0 of 14 paths hit the governed register; 2327 changed lines, under the 3000 human-merge threshold; ordinary queue landing applies once checks are green. The tier here is owed by the published-schema face, not by a governed path.
- Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-06T16:19Z: 62 total — 23 success, 8 skipped, 2 failure (named above), 29 in progress (Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check ×4, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI). The in-progress runs are not read as green.

### ④ Design judgment

- Schema file against the ruling it implements: the maintainer's direction on #30794 (a prefix at install to avoid duplicates) and ADR-0048 §3.5's deferred rename-on-install, under the spec consent of 6688079820. The two optional keys are the minimal request/response shape for that: the request names the namespace, the answer records the provenance only when a rename happened. The describe for `targetNamespace` states the rule it is judged by (`manifest.namespace`), the reserved set, and the default — all three are true in the code (:480, :488, :496). The describe for `sourceNamespace` says "present when the copy was renamed" and the code matches (:721, and `targetNamespace` equal to the source is treated as no rename, :540).
- First consumer: the install-local door, which forwards the key and records `installedFrom.namespace` (door :2222, :3999, :4038), pinned by the door's tests. A managed install can never reach the rename (door :1818). The parity anchor shows the second door (duplicate) yields identical items, so the published semantics "the rename `duplicatePackage` applies" in the describe is a measured claim, not prose.
- The `check:generated` artifacts and the reference page match the schema. Holds.

## Contract review · delta

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a39d3108790bca29ff42fe3de60bbb2079a01bb6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/lint-root-preload.testkit.ts (read at the head), scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs (read at the head and at origin/main `acd190b2`, the #30969 merge that holds the source-reach half)

Delta over record 6689730882 (head `8b377514…`). The new head's sole parent is `8b377514f88d5e040ca98878bcde829b0fb834a4`, the sha that record reviewed. `git diff 8b377514 a39d3108 --stat` is exactly one file, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`, +2/−0: a one-line comment ("Pays the lint root's first load at collection, never inside a clocked case.") and a module-top `import './lint-root-preload.testkit.js';`, placed first, before the `vitest` import. Commit `test(metadata-protocol): unmanaged-install test pays the lint root at collection`. Nothing under `packages/spec/**`, no source file, no docs, no changeset moved, so every judgment in ①, ②, ④ of the prior record stands unchanged; this delta re-reads only the one landing blocker it named.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The remedy is the one the gate asks for, spelled the sibling way.** `lint-root-preload.testkit.ts` exists on the head and is a test-only file whose single statement is `import '@objectstack/lint';` at module scope (its docblock names exactly this case: `loadFormLayoutLint` in metadata-diagnostics.ts, resolved through `lint/dist/index.js`). 41 other `packages/metadata-protocol/src/*.test.ts` files import it with the identical relative line, so the PR's test now matches its siblings rather than inventing a second spelling. **Confirmed.**
- **The source-reach half credits a relative hop.** Read at `acd190b2` (the merged #30969 script, which is what the lane runs on the merge ref; the PR branch's own copy predates it): `sourceReachFindings` walks the test's collection-time reach inside the package, unions every reached file's module-scope loads into `warm`, and drops a finding when `warm.has(spec)`. The testkit is a same-package relative static import, so `@objectstack/lint` is in `warm` and the `import('@objectstack/lint')` at metadata-diagnostics.ts:494 no longer reports. The script's own `source-reach-warm` control fixture pins this exact shape ("a load another reached file already pays during collection was reported" is a self-test failure). The clocked-window half is unaffected (the test file still has no dynamic import of its own). **The flagged finding is answered by the rule's own words, not by a workaround.**
- **Test behaviour otherwise unchanged.** A side-effect import that only loads a package already loaded lazily by the source under test moves where the first load is paid (collection, unclocked) and yields the same module instance to the protocol's later `import()`. No case, assertion, fixture or timeout in the file moved; the diff has no other hunk. **Confirmed.**
- Spec hunk, authorable surface, docs, changeset: untouched since `8b377514`, so ① of 6689730882 holds as written.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. A test-only commit moves no package's grade.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The prior record's landing blocker (Test-source alias gate, source-reach half, on this test file) is addressed on this head by the change above. Whether the lane itself reports green is a CI fact, recorded below.
- The should-fix on the prose error code (`INVALID_REQUEST` vs the `VALIDATION_ERROR` the planner refusals actually answer) is not touched by this commit and stays open as a should-fix, not a contract must-fix.
- Q6 (1f and a renamed copy) unchanged; still safe to land without the ruling.
- Check-runs on `a39d3108` at 2026-11-06T16:29Z: 42 registered — 20 success, 7 skipped, 0 failure, 15 in progress (Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace / debt ledger / consumer gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates). **`Lint · CI, release & engine gates` completed green at 16:28:40Z** (it was the red lane on `8b377514`, failing at the Test-source alias gate step; it took the same ~6 min this time). No red on the head. The `Lint & Repo Gates` aggregator and the rest of the prior head's 62 runs have not registered yet; the 15 in-progress runs are not read as green.
